report.source_text: MRI of the brain (figure 1) was done, which revealed a thick-walled peripherally enhancing lesion of size ~45×43×37 mm in the right parietal lobe in the peritrigonal location. The lesion wall had crenulated margins with intracavitary projections, which showed blooming on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and diffusion restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). The core of the lesion was hyperintense, which was suppressed on a fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequence. Marked perilesional oedema was also seen on T2-weighted/FLAIR imaging with surrounding mass effect. On magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), raised lipid lactates and trehalose were seen. Based on imaging findings, a diagnosis of the fungal abscess was made.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Fungal brain abscess due to Aspergillus following COVID-19 pneumonia
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 62-year-old man with controlled diabetes was hospitalized for moderate COVID-19 pneumonia (CT severity score 15/25) requiring 30 days of hospitalization including 10 days in ICU with supplemental oxygen and methylprednisolone 20 mg IV twice daily for 6 days. He was discharged 10 days prior to current presentation with SpO2 92% on room air. Post-COVID immunosuppression predisposed him to opportunistic fungal infection. He presented with acute neurological symptoms (altered behaviour, speech slurring, left-sided weakness) for 6 days. Initial laboratory tests were normal except for mildly raised alkaline phosphatase and D-dimer. MRI brain performed on admission revealed a thick-walled peripherally enhancing lesion (45×43×37 mm) in the right parietal lobe at the peritrigonal location with imaging features highly suggestive of fungal abscess: crenulated margins, intracavitary projections, blooming on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI), diffusion restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and marked perilesional edema with mass effect. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) showed raised lipid lactates and trehalose, further supporting fungal abscess diagnosis. Imaging-guided aspiration/biopsy was performed to obtain pus for microbiological confirmation. Culture of the pus grew Aspergillus organism, confirming the diagnosis of fungal brain abscess. Concurrent CT thorax showed peripheral pulmonary cavities, segmental right pulmonary artery thrombus, and diffuse parenchymal fibrosis consistent with post-COVID sequelae.
